concept.tagline: Multiplexing strongly typed binary Protobuf messages over persistent HTTP/2 streams with deadline propagation and per-stream flow control.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of gRPC—from 5-byte length-prefixed framing and HTTP/2 trailers to deadline propagation, backpressure, and L7 load balancing.

spark.summary: gRPC multiplexes strongly typed Protobuf messages over persistent HTTP/2 streams, supporting unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and full-duplex bidirectional RPCs.

spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** REST/JSON over HTTP/1.1 burns CPU parsing text keys and stalls behind connection-pool limits.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts HTTP/2 Stream Framing & Cascading grpc-timeout Propagation (API Gateway -> Pricing Svc -> Fraud ML Svc); Why L4 Pins gRPC — And How L7 Envoy Multiplexes Per-RPC (gRPC Client Pod -> Envoy L7 Proxy -> Backend Pod 1 -> New Pod 2 (HPA)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Pick the RPC protocol based on client environment, caching needs, and streaming requirements. Because gRPC multiplexes 100+ concurrent streams over a single persistent TCP connection, a naive **L4 load balancer** routes all RPCs to the first pod—leaving newly autoscaled pods idle!

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore production guides on gRPC L7 load balancing, timeout budgets, and safe Protobuf schema evolution.

learningJourney.title: What is gRPC & How It Maps onto HTTP/2
learningJourney.explanation:
REST/JSON over HTTP/1.1 burns CPU parsing text keys and stalls behind connection-pool limits. **gRPC** serializes strongly typed `.proto` contracts into binary **Protocol Buffers (`proto3`)** over persistent **HTTP/2** connections.

Each RPC maps to an HTTP/2 stream: initial `HEADERS` carry `:path` (`/pkg.Svc/Method`) and `grpc-timeout` (`500m`), `DATA` frames carry **5-byte length-prefixed Protobuf messages** (1B compressed flag + 4B big-endian length + payload), and trailing `HEADERS` (`END_STREAM`) deliver `grpc-status` (`0` OK, `4` DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, `14` UNAVAILABLE).

sectionDiagram.title: HTTP/2 Stream Framing & Cascading grpc-timeout Propagation
sectionDiagram.summary: gRPC propagates remaining deadline budgets across hops so downstream services abort wasted work immediately.

learningJourney.title: Why Binary Framing, Backpressure & Deadlines Matter
learningJourney.explanation: Protobuf + HPACK cuts payload size by **40–70%** and serialization CPU by **3–5x** vs. JSON. Crucially, HTTP/2 `WINDOW_UPDATE` frames (64 KiB default window) provide automatic per-stream **backpressure** so a slow consumer never OOMs a fast streaming producer.

ideas.title: Four RPC Modes
ideas.description: Unary (1->1), Server-Streaming (1->N, e.g., LLM tokens), Client-Streaming (N->1, telemetry), and Bidirectional (N<->N, real-time ASR).

ideas.title: Schema Evolution with `reserved`
ideas.description: Never reuse deleted Protobuf field numbers; mark them `reserved 3; reserved "legacy_id";` and gate PRs with `buf breaking`.

learningJourney.title: Where gRPC Excels (and Where REST/WebSockets Fit Better)
learningJourney.explanation: Use gRPC for internal polyglot microservices and streaming; avoid it for direct browser calls without a proxy or cacheable public REST APIs.

benefits: Auto-generated typed clients (Go, Java, Rust, Python), built-in deadlines, and 3–10x smaller payloads.
costs: Binary payloads require `.proto` descriptors (`grpcurl`) to inspect on the wire.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Bidirectional & LLM Token Streaming
benefits: Full-duplex streams over one TLS connection with automatic HTTP/2 flow-control backpressure.
costs: TCP packet loss causes head-of-line blocking across all multiplexed streams on that socket.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Direct Browser Calls Without Proxy
benefits: Standard `fetch()`/REST or WebSockets work natively without Envoy gRPC-Web translation.
costs: Browsers do not expose raw HTTP/2 trailers (`grpc-status`) to JavaScript.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Streaming Chunks Instead of Giant Payloads & Protobuf Safety
learningJourney.explanation: gRPC enforces a default **4 MB** max message size (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). Instead of raising it to 100 MB, convert large list responses into **server-streaming RPCs** emitting 64–256 KiB chunks, and align client `keepalive_time_ms` (`>=60s`) with server enforcement to avoid `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` disconnects.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: gRPC vs. REST/JSON vs. GraphQL
learningJourney.explanation: Pick the RPC protocol based on client environment, caching needs, and streaming requirements.

benefits: Highest internal throughput, native bidirectional streaming, and strict deadline propagation.
costs: Requires L7 load balancing (Envoy/Istio) because L4 pins long-lived HTTP/2 connections.

benefits: Universal browser/curl support, OpenAPI ecosystem, and native CDN `Cache-Control` caching.
costs: Verbose text serialization and no built-in bidirectional streaming.

benefits: Client-driven field selection preventing mobile over-fetching across domain graphs.
costs: Query-parsing overhead and weaker fit for binary streaming.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Topology: L7 Envoy Load Balancing for HTTP/2
learningJourney.explanation: Because gRPC multiplexes 100+ concurrent streams over a single persistent TCP connection, a naive **L4 load balancer** routes all RPCs to the first pod—leaving newly autoscaled pods idle! Production clusters deploy **L7 proxies (Envoy/Istio)** or client-side `round_robin` via headless Kubernetes Services.

sectionDiagram.title: Why L4 Pins gRPC — And How L7 Envoy Multiplexes Per-RPC

cards.label: L4 Trap
cards.detail: L4 balances per TCP connection, pinning 100% of traffic to old pods after HPA scale-out.

cards.label: L7 / Headless Fix
cards.detail: Envoy L7 or client-side round_robin over headless DNS spreads individual RPCs evenly.

cards.label: Keepalive Alignment
cards.detail: Match client keepalive >=60s with server limits to prevent GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM.

sectionDiagram.summary: L7-aware load balancing (or client-side round_robin) is mandatory to scale gRPC horizontally across pods.

knowledgeCheck.question: You autoscale a gRPC backend from 2 pods to 6 pods behind a Kubernetes `ClusterIP` L4 Service, but the 4 new pods receive zero traffic. Why?

options.text: gRPC multiplexes all RPCs over one long-lived HTTP/2 TCP connection, and L4 load balancers only balance at TCP connection setup
options.feedback: Correct: use an L7 proxy (Envoy/Istio) or client-side `round_robin` with a headless service (`clusterIP: None`).
Protobuf is just the payload encoding; HTTP/2 multiplexing is the root cause of L4 pinning.

options.text: Because `grpc-timeout` blocks new pods from registering

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
